**What "anonymous189.2033979700" means**

That packageId isn't a real mod ID — it's a placeholder RimSort (and RimWorld itself) generates when it finds a mod folder on disk but can't read a valid `About.xml` from it (missing file, empty file, or corrupted). The `2033979700` is the Steam Workshop item ID pulled from the folder name, so you can identify it directly:

`https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2033979700`

If that page says "This item is unavailable because the author removed it" (or similar), the author deleted/unpublished it from Workshop. Steam does **not** clean up the local folder for you in that case — you're left with an orphaned directory that has no metadata, hence "no versions, no description."

**Why this causes ~140 'Could not load reference' errors for PRF_ defs**

`PRF_` is the defName prefix used by the **Project RimFactory** family of mods (Core, Extended, Extended Production, Drugs, Garden, Storage, SK, Arcology, etc. — packageId roots like `spdskatr.rimfactory` / `notfood.projectrimfactory` depending on fork). Something in your load order is referencing `PRF_` defs (either an add-on/patch mod, or one of the other PRF family mods expecting Core), but the mod that actually *defines* those `PRF_` defs is the one that just died — this orphaned anonymous folder is it, or it's a dependency of it. Since its About.xml/Defs never loaded properly, every other mod's XML patches or direct references to `PRF_...` defNames fail to resolve, producing one error per broken reference — easily 100+ if it's Core plus several extensions all pointing at missing base defs.

**Smallest fix, in order of importance**

1. **Confirm identity via the Workshop link above.** This tells you exactly which PRF component it was.
2. **Remove the orphaned folder manually.** Go to your Steam Workshop mods directory (`...\steamapps\workshop\content\294100\2033979700`) and delete it — Steam won't do this automatically for a delisted item. Also unsubscribe it in RimSort/Steam if it still shows as subscribed.
3. **Re-add the real mod.** If it was Project RimFactory Core (or one of its extensions) and it's genuinely gone from Workshop, get it from a maintained fork/mirror — the actively updated ones for 1.6 are usually under the "Project RimFactory Revived" or Neronix17/SmashPhil GitHub releases, not the original dead Workshop page. Subscribe/install that instead, keeping the same folder structure so packageId matches what other PRF-family mods expect (`spdskatr.rimfactory` is the common Core packageId — check the other PRF mods' About.xml `<modDependencies>` to see exactly which packageId they're expecting).
4. **Load order:** once the real Core is back, make sure it loads before any PRF extension/addon mods (Extended, Garden, Drugs, SK, etc.) — RimSort's Community Rules already encode this dependency chain, so if Core's packageId is correct, RimSort should auto-sort it correctly.

After that, re-run and the `PRF_` reference errors should disappear as a block, since they all trace back to the same missing definer.

If you paste the actual list of PRF-prefixed mods you have installed (or the exact error lines), I can narrow down which specific fork/version you need and check load order against it.

This error pattern (dozens/all filth defs failing with "trashType must be declared") isn't caused by one filth def being wrong — it's caused by an **abstract base def being overwritten**.

**Why it happens:**
In 1.6, Ludeon added a required `trashType` field to the vanilla abstract def `FilthBase` (which almost every FilthDef in the game, vanilla and modded, inherits from via `ParentName="FilthBase"`). If a mod ships its own copy of `Filth.xml` (or any file containing a `<FilthDef Name="FilthBase" Abstract="True">` def) that predates 1.6 and hasn't been updated to include `trashType`, and that mod's file loads **after** Core, it silently overwrites the vanilla abstract def with the old one. Every filth def that inherits from `FilthBase` — including vanilla ones — then loses `trashType`, so you get one error per filth def in the entire load order, not just the offending mod's own.

**How to find the culprit:**
It's a mod that predates 1.6 and includes a full/duplicated copy of vanilla's Filth defs as a template (common in older filth-adding mods and some frameworks) rather than just adding new FilthDefs. Look in RimSort's log or the mod's `Defs` folder for a file defining `FilthBase` outside of Core.

I don't have your actual active mod list in this session, so I can't name the exact packageId with certainty — can you paste your mod list (or the RimSort log snippet around the first "trashType" error, which shows the defining mod)? That will tell me exactly which one is shipping the stale `FilthBase`.

**The fix once identified**, in order of preference:
1. Update that mod to its current 1.6 release if one exists — the author has almost certainly patched their `FilthBase` copy to include `trashType`.
2. If no update exists, delete/comment out the `<FilthDef Name="FilthBase" Abstract="True">...</FilthDef>` block from that mod's XML so it stops overriding Core's version, and let its own filth defs inherit from vanilla's `FilthBase` instead.
3. As a last resort, load that mod **before** Core in the list (not recommended, breaks other things) — better to just strip the duplicate abstract def.

That error means some loaded mod has a def (usually a building or another ResearchProjectDef) listing `VFE_IndustrialGenerators` as a research prerequisite/link, but the def itself — which actually lives in **Vanilla Furniture Expanded** (the original, not one of the Expanded-series spin-offs) — isn't present when defs get resolved.

**What's wrong**
The `VFE_` prefix belongs to the base "Vanilla Furniture Expanded" mod by Oskar Potocki / Vanilla Expanded team. `IndustrialGenerators` is a research project it defines (generator-type furniture is gated behind it). Something else in your list depends on that research existing.

**Why**
Either:
1. **Vanilla Furniture Expanded** isn't installed/subscribed at all, or
2. It's installed but **disabled** in your mod list, or
3. You have a different VFE-family mod (e.g., a "Vanilla Furniture Expanded — [something]" addon) that expects the base VFE mod as a hard dependency, and that dependency got missed.

Load order is not the issue here — Def resolution happens after all mods finish loading, so as long as the mod defining `VFE_IndustrialGenerators` is anywhere in the active list, the reference resolves regardless of position. This is a **missing/disabled mod** problem, not a sequencing problem.

**Smallest fix**
- Check your mod list for "Vanilla Furniture Expanded" (packageId `OskarPotocki.VanillaFurnitureExpanded` — verify against your local About.xml since I can't inspect your install).
- If it's not there: subscribe/install it and enable it.
- If it's there but unchecked: enable it.
- If it's genuinely not there and you don't want it: the real fix is removing/disabling whichever mod is throwing the reference, since it's a hard dependency on VFE.

If you can paste the exact mod that's throwing the warning (the log line usually names the mod above the "could not resolve reference" message), I can confirm which one is missing the dependency rather than guessing.

Short answer: that specific line usually isn't pointing at a single "broken" mod at all — you likely don't need to hunt one down.

**What it actually is:**
`Fallback handler could not load library ... data-XXXXXXXX.dll` is Mono/Unity's debugger trying to attach symbol/stack-trace info to a *dynamically generated* in-memory assembly. Harmony (used by nearly every C# mod) creates one such dynamic module every time it builds a patch — the module gets an auto-generated name like `data-1a2b3c4d.dll`. There's no real file on disk with that name, so Mono logs a harmless "couldn't load" fallback message. With a large modlist you can easily get hundreds of these, one per patched method, and they're background noise — not an error causing your actual crashes/red text.

**Why "which mod" is the wrong question here:**
Since it fires for *every* Harmony-patched assembly, the line itself carries no mod identity. It's not like a normal exception line that names an assembly/class.

**What would actually let me point to a specific mod:**
- If these lines are immediately followed by a real exception (a red "Could not create instance..." or "MissingMethodException" etc.) *right after* one of them, that adjacent stack trace is what names the mod — the dll line itself is just noise before/after it.
- If you're seeing an actual load failure for a *named native library* (something like `libSkiaSharp.dll`, `steam_api64.dll`, `AssetStudio.dll`, etc.) rather than a `data-XXXXXXXX.dll` hash, that's different — that's a genuine native-plugin mod (e.g., mods bundling image/DB libraries) failing to find its .dll, usually from a bad extraction or missing architecture-specific binary.

**Smallest next step:** don't chase the `data-XXXXXXXX.dll` lines themselves — search your Player.log for the nearest actual `Exception` or red-error text near them, or for a *named* (non-hash) library filename. Paste that surrounding text or your mod list and I can tell you which packageId it traces to.

A few things worth knowing about **While You're Up** (Uuugggg.WhileYoureUp):

- Uuugggg keeps his mods (Smart Farming, Fishing, While You're Up, etc.) updated fairly promptly each version, so a 1.6-flagged release is plausible and generally trustworthy.

Wrong order has historically caused colonists to ignore "while you're up" pickups or occasionally throw job-driver errors.
- It also plays with any mod that changes hauling/stack-carry behavior (e.g., Combat Extended's inventory changes) — no confirmed 1.6 incompatibility there that I know of, just something to watch for if you run CE.

**Quarry should load after Alpha Biomes.**

- **Source:** RimSort Community Rules (not the mod authors — neither Quarry's nor Alpha Biomes' About.xml specifies this dependency directly).
- **Why:** Quarry scans the active mod list at load to build its pool of spawnable minerals/resources/chunks. Alpha Biomes (packageId `sarg.alphabiomes`) adds new terrain types, rock types, and resources tied to its custom biomes. If Quarry loads first, it finishes building its resource table before those new terrain/rock defs exist, so Alpha Biomes' materials never get added to what the quarry can produce — not a hard error, just a silent content gap (or occasional def-injection warnings depending on Quarry's fork).
- **Fix:** In your mod list, move Quarry below Alpha Biomes (and generally below other biome/terrain-adding mods like Alpha Animals' terrain content, Geological Landforms, etc., since the same "load after terrain-adding mods" rule applies broadly to Quarry).

Note: I don't have an owner-specific incident on file for this exact pair — this is purely the RimSort community rule. If you've hit a concrete error/log line with these two, let me know and I'll fold that in as the higher-priority source.

No — they conflict and shouldn't be run together.

**Why:** Both mods do the same job: they patch RimWorld's camera controller to allow extended zoom range and adjustable camera settings (zoom speed, angle, etc.). They each hook into the same base-game camera driver class (`CameraDriver`/zoom limits) via Harmony patches or direct field edits. Running both means two mods fighting over the same settings and patch targets, which typically causes:
- Zoom limits reverting or behaving erratically (one mod's limits overriding the other's on tick/settings-change)
- Harmony patch conflicts/errors in the log referencing `CameraDriver.CurrentZoom` or similar
- Duplicate mod-settings menus for the same functionality, with only one actually taking effect

Neither author lists the other as a required dependency — they're alternatives, not complements.

**Fix:** Pick one, not both. Practical guidance:
- If you want more configuration options (zoom speed curves, dolly, etc.), keep **Camera+** (packageId `krkr.rimworld.camera` — verify against your actual local copy, but it's the more feature-rich of the two).
- If you just want a simple "increase max zoom out" toggle with minimal footprint, keep **Simple Camera Setting** (packageId typically `taranchuk.simplecameracontrol` or similar — check your local About.xml).

Disable the other in RimSort/mod list. There's no load-order fix here since it's a functional overlap, not a load-order issue — enabling both will not resolve cleanly regardless of order.

## What's happening

RimWorld's own `ThingDef.ConfigErrors` check flags any def that is `passability="Impassable"` but has `fillPercent` set below 1.0. The check exists because full impassability implies full cover, and a low `fillPercent` implies partial cover — the two are logically inconsistent, so the game logs a config error at startup.

Signs and Comments hits this because its sign/plaque ThingDefs are set `Impassable` (so pawns don't walk through/stand on them like a solid post) but use a thin `fillPercent` (e.g. 0.2–0.5) so the graphic doesn't visually claim a full cell. That mismatch is exactly what the check complains about — hence 18 errors, one per sign variant.

## Is it actually a problem?

No. This is a well-known cosmetic-only warning, not a functional bug. It doesn't stop the mod from loading, doesn't break pathing, and doesn't affect gameplay. It shows up in a bunch of decorative/sign-type mods across the workshop for the same reason (thin objects that authors still want fully solid).

## Smallest fix

Don't edit the mod's own XML directly — any change there gets wiped on the next Signs and Comments update. Instead:

1. **Easiest — just ignore it.** In RimSort, mark these as known/filtered warnings so they stop showing red. No functional downside.
2. **If you want it gone for real:** make a tiny local patch mod (a folder under your Mods directory with just an `About.xml` + `Patches/Patch.xml`) that either:
   - sets `<fillPercent>1</fillPercent>` on the affected sign defs (accepts that signs now count as full cover — minor, cosmetic tradeoff), or
   - changes `<passability>Impassable</passability>` to `<passability>PassThroughOnly</passability>` (pawns still can't stand on/reserve the tile, error disappears, but pawns can walk *through* the sign tile instead of pathing around it — closest to no visible behavior change for a decorative object).

Either patch approach targets `ThingDef` where `passability == Impassable` and the defName pattern used by the mod (I don't have the mod's exact packageId or defNames memorized with certainty, so double-check the actual defName prefix in the mod's `Defs/ThingDefs_*.xml` before writing the `PatchOperationConditional`).

**Bottom line:** these 18 errors are harmless noise from a fillPercent/passability mismatch in the mod's own sign defs. Safe to ignore/filter; only patch it yourself if the red text bothers you.

Nothing is crashing — this is a logging verbosity setting, not a broken game.

**What's happening:** Unity's logger has a per-message-type "stack trace" setting (`Application.SetStackTraceLogType`). By default RimWorld only attaches stack traces to Warnings/Errors/Exceptions, not to plain `Log.Message()` calls. If you're seeing a trace under *every* line including plain info messages, something has flipped the trace level for the "Log" type to Full/ScriptOnly. That's almost always one of:

1. **A debug/dev-tools mod left in "verbose" mode** — things like HugsLib-based debug helpers, a log-viewer mod, or a performance/profiling mod that calls `SetStackTraceLogType` for its own diagnostics but does it globally, so it affects everyone else's log lines too.
2. **Dev Mode + "verbose logging" checkbox** in RimWorld's own options (Options → uncheck "Verbose logging"/dev toggles) — if you have Dev Mode on, check whether a "verbose" or "log everything" checkbox is ticked there or in a dev-tools mod's settings.
3. **RimSort/launcher flag** — running with `-logfile` plus certain Player launch args doesn't normally do this, so it's less likely, but worth ruling out if you customized launch parameters.

**Smallest fix:** it's cosmetic — it doesn't mean anything is actually erroring, it just makes the log huge and hard to read. To stop it:
- Turn off Dev Mode (or its verbose-log option) if enabled.
- If you're running a debug-utility mod (anything billed as a "log tool," "debug helper," "performance monitor"), open its mod settings and look for a verbose/full-stack-trace toggle and disable it.
- If you don't recognize which one, disable debug/dev-tool mods one at a time and re-launch; the one whose removal makes plain Info lines stop carrying traces is the culprit.

**UI Not Included (`unlimitedhugs.uinotincluded` — actually packageId is `uinotincludedteam.uinotincluded` in current versions) should load *after* Smart Speed (`legodude17.smartspeed`).**

Why: UI Not Included works by scanning the screen for UI buttons/gizmos added by other mods (speed controls, alert icons, etc.) and re-organizing/hiding them into its overflow menu. It needs those buttons to already exist in the game's UI systems when it initializes so it can detect and manage them. Smart Speed adds its own speed-control buttons to the top UI bar — if UI Not Included loads before it, it can miss those buttons on the initial pass and fail to manage/collapse them correctly (buttons overlapping or not appearing in the UI Not Included dropdown).

Smallest fix: in your load order, move UI Not Included below Smart Speed (it doesn't need to be adjacent — just anywhere after it, typically grouped with other "UI management" mods near the end of your UI/QoL block).

I don't have a specific incident log entry from you for this pair, so this is based on the general community/author guidance for UI Not Included (it explicitly says in its own docs to load it late, after mods that add buttons). If you've observed a concrete conflict or the opposite ordering worked for your list, that observation should override this.

**XML Extensions (zal.xmlextensions) loads before Vanilla Storytellers Expanded – Winston Waves (VanillaExpanded.VSEWinstonWaves).**

Why: XML Extensions is a patch-operation framework — it adds the custom XML instructions (list ops, node checks, etc.) that other mods' patches call. Winston Waves, like most Vanilla Expanded storyteller/faction/etc. mods, uses those XML Extensions operations in its own patches, so the framework has to already be loaded and processed first or Winston Waves' patches fail to apply (usually surfacing as patch errors or missing defs at startup rather than a crash).

General rule of thumb this follows: frameworks (Harmony, HugsLib, XML Extensions, CombatExtended framework, etc.) sit near the top of the load order, above the content mods that consume them.

**Save Our Ship 2 before Rimatomics.**

- SOS2 (`kentington.saveourship2`) needs to load first because Rimatomics ships a built-in compatibility patch that adds SOS2-specific reactor/shield-shunt integration for its nuclear reactors. That patch checks for SOS2's defs at load time, so if Rimatomics loads before SOS2, the patch either fails silently or throws def-not-found / patch-target errors on startup.
- Rimatomics (packageId is typically listed as `atomicrepublic.rimatomics` — double-check the exact string in your own About.xml/RimSort listing since it's occasionally miswritten) should sit **after** SOS2 and after Harmony/HugsLib, but doesn't need to be adjacent — just anywhere below SOS2 in the list.

If you're seeing actual errors (not just asking preemptively), paste the log lines — I can tell you if it's this exact patch-order issue or something else (e.g., a Harmony transpiler conflict between the two mods' reactor code, which is a separate, less common problem).
